fixtures.description: Same canonical creation digest under offline, peer-hosted and authoritative policies.
Reparenting changes containment only; controller, authority and network declaration remain unchanged.
Declared client input is accepted as intent without directly mutating authoritative state.
Input from a principal that does not control the Thing is rejected.
Duplicate/stale input sequence is rejected.
Only current simulation authority can author declared replicated state.
Authority transfer bumps epoch and stale old-authority state is rejected.
Changing per-peer relevance does not alter containment or Thing existence.
Reconnect may change transport peer ID while preserving principal/controller/Thing semantics.
Known-unloaded state updates coalesce to the latest bounded delivery and apply on restore.
Reliable semantic event to an unloaded target deduplicates and is delivered once on restore.
Pending network deliveries for unloaded targets are hard-bounded.
Tombstoned Thing rejects new runtime network delivery.
Peer-host migration preserves Thing identity and increments authority epoch.
Transport/runtime identifiers such as peer_id/WebSocket/RPC/NodePath are rejected from canonical network data.
Network topology/session activity preserves asset source/audio/provenance records and canonical digest.
Non-offline multiplayer admission requires mediated multiplayer capability/service policy.
Runtime replication declaration contains no canonical collaboration transaction/conflict vocabulary.
Undeclared replicated state/event loci are rejected.
Peer-host migration operation is not silently available under dedicated-authoritative policy.

notes: Fixtures test semantic separability and hostile boundaries, not real network latency or wire compatibility.
Source/audio/provenance semantics are protected and must not be rewritten by topology projection.
